title: HP-MDR: High-performance and Portable Data Refactoring and Progressive Retrieval with Advanced GPUs
problem: Scientific data management lacks GPU-accelerated progressive compression; existing methods are CPU-based and leave GPU performance potential untapped for heterogeneous systems
motivation: Scientific simulations produce vast data; GPU-accelerated progressive methods enabling on-demand retrieval could dramatically reduce data movement cost and I/O latency
method: The system moves data compression from CPUs to GPUs, which can process many calculations in parallel. It combines two compression techniques—bitplane encoding (breaking numbers into individual bit layers) and lossless encoding (preserving all original data)—arranged in a pipeline so different stages run together for speed. Instead of always retrieving complete data, users retrieve it progressively, stopping when they have 'good enough' quality. Users specify their acceptable level of error, and the system delivers compressed data meeting that quality threshold.
key_novelty: GPU-accelerated progressive compression of scientific data where users control precision during retrieval.
contributions: GPU-optimized bitplane and lossless encoding stages
Pipeline optimization for large-scale data processing
QoI-driven error control for data retrieval
13.68x throughput improvement in data refactoring, 6.31x in retrieval vs SOTA
limitations: GPU memory constraints for very large datasets; QoI error model specificity not detailed; evaluation on specific GPU types
